narrative.overview:
Bridgecast looks like a video editor's workspace, not a slide app and not a floating card UI. One window is divided into docked panels by 1px rules: a 52px header bar, a Decks panel (288px), the Program column, and a 352px right panel with the tabs Info (Notes) and Controls (Up next, Transition, Deck settings, Output, Network). The Program column is monitor, one slim transport bar, and a slide strip as a timeline. The header holds Home and the open-event tabs; Home is the event browser (Recent, All, Archive). Nothing floats except the Settings dialog (Appearance, Sound, About) and menus.

One colour does all the signalling: the user's accent (soft orange by default; violet, blue, rose, sand, or a custom colour, chosen in Settings). It marks everything active or on air: LIVE, FROZEN, BLACK and KV tags, the monitor ring, the live slide ring, pressed hold buttons, the current deck row. There is no red or amber. Filled means on air, outlined means Next, a pressed hold is tinted and outlined.

Type is Geist for words and Cascadia Mono, then Consolas, for every number, count, key cap and slide number, with tabular figures on. Both themes ship; the default follows the OS. The monitor and slide letterboxes stay black. The Bridgecast logo dot (--brand-signal, #f26f1c) is fixed and never follows the accent.
keyCharacteristics: Flat docked panels, 1px rules, no cards, no panel shadows.
Radii 3, 4 and 6px; round only for switches, sliders, progress bars and swatches.
One state colour, the user's accent. Filled = on air, outlined = Next.
One scale: control heights 32/40/52, panel inset 20, gaps 4/8/12/16/24, type 12/14/16.
Words in Geist, numbers in mono, tabular figures on.
Cool near-neutral greys in light and dark themes; the monitor stays black.

rules.name: The One State Colour Rule
rules.body: Anything active or on air uses the accent and nothing else. Never add a second chromatic colour for state. Errors and warnings are ink, weight and an icon, not a hue.

rules.name: The Fill Means On Air Rule
rules.body: A filled accent tag or a solid 2px accent ring means the audience sees it. An outlined tag or a 45% ring means Next. A pressed hold button is a tinted fill with an accent border. State is never colour alone.

rules.name: The Cool Neutral Rule
rules.body: Greys may carry a faint cool cast, never a strong hue. The accent is the only saturated colour on screen besides slide content.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Every count, position, resolution, key cap and slide number is mono; every sentence is Geist.

rules.name: The Flat Docked Rule
rules.body: Group with 1px rules and tonal steps. No cards, no floating panels; the one real shadow (--pop-shadow) is for the Settings dialog and menus.

dos: Do use the accent for every active or on-air mark and for nothing else.
Do say state with an icon, a shape and an accessible name as well as colour.
Do keep to the one scale: radius 3/4/6, heights 32/40/52, inset 20, type 12/14/16.
Do read every colour from tokens.css variables so both themes, every accent and custom colours stay correct.
Do keep the monitor, letterboxes and standby card black in both themes.
Do keep the transport bar to one row under the monitor.
Do respond to the Program column's width (container queries), not the window, when hiding key caps.
donts: Don't add a second state colour (no red tally, no amber Next); differentiate with fill versus outline.
Don't put a dot beside a status word; use a tag with an icon.
Don't float panels, add card shadows, or round navigation into pills.
Don't introduce a fourth radius or a new control height.
Don't put the operator's Fade under prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't show a slide before its image is decoded.
Don't let --brand-signal follow the accent; it is the logo dot only.
